claim_text: Under sustained GNSS denial the diagnosis reports nominal for the entire fault window and never names gps_fault, while the GPS trust coefficient reads 0.9767.
definition: 'never names' = gps_fault is not the top cause at any tick after onset; trust is the per-node coefficient from csia/trust_engine/engine.py.
baseline: Arm A (spoof, fix retained) on the same flight: gps_fault leads within 1.44 s.
counter_evidence: None found. Arm B top_cause_occupancy_after_onset shows nominal at 1.0 for 1000 ticks.
alternative_explanation: The trust coefficient could be high because the fault is genuinely small. Excluded: the injected fault removes the fix entirely, and arm A with a smaller position error does produce the lead.

claim_text: The mechanism is structural: with the GPS physics feature gated out, no active feature distinguishes nominal from gps_fault, so their log posterior ratio equals the log prior ratio exactly.
definition: 'no active feature distinguishes' = (LOW(nominal) symmetric-difference LOW(gps_fault)) intersect ACTIVE is empty. 'exactly' = P3 of research/math-paper/FORMAL_CORE.md.
baseline: Any tick where phys_gps is active: the pair is distinguishable and the ratio moves.
counter_evidence: None. The identity is verified symbolically and to 8.882e-16 numerically.
alternative_explanation: The posterior could be pinned for a numerical reason rather than a structural one. Excluded: the symbolic check holds for arbitrary positive priors and likelihoods.

claim_text: An independent structural checker, importing no CSIA module and no part of the support-aware implementation, agrees with the production discriminating-term analysis on 378,000 of 378,000 tick-by-pair comparisons.
definition: 9 scenarios x 1500 ticks x 28 unordered hypothesis pairs. Agreement = identical term sets.
counter_evidence: One disagreement class exists in theory (c == 0.5 makes the two definitions differ) and was NOT observed: 0 degenerate cases in 378,000.
alternative_explanation: Agreement could be circular if the checker read production's answer. Excluded: the checker's only inputs are the committed signature YAML and an active-set export that carries no support analysis, and a test asserts no csia module is imported.

claim_text: gps_fault|nominal is the only hypothesis pair in the deterministic scenario catalogue that ever becomes structurally indistinguishable.
definition: Over all 9 scenarios and all 28 pairs, collapsed_pairs is empty except for this pair.
baseline: All 28 pairs evaluated, not only the pair of interest.
counter_evidence: None in this catalogue. The catalogue is 9 scenarios on the bench simulator and is not a claim about all flights.
alternative_explanation: Other pairs might collapse under gate combinations the catalogue does not produce. Not excluded; the claim is scoped to the catalogue.

claim_text: The pair is also structurally indistinguishable for 76 ticks at the start of EVERY scenario, including clean flight, before the GPS physics gate opens.
definition: Ticks 0-75 of every arm; phys_gps gate is 0 for t <= 3.0 s by construction (csia/prediction/comparator.py: gvalid * (ticks > 3.0)).
baseline: The clean arm is its own baseline: 76 ticks pinned with no fault present.
counter_evidence: None. This is a startup-window property, not a fault.
alternative_explanation: This could be read as a defect. It is not: the gate is deliberately closed during the smoother warm-up, and the failsafe is not armed for the first 10 s (FailsafeConfig.arm_time).

claim_text: Under GNSS fix loss the pair is additionally indistinguishable for 200 consecutive ticks (8.0 s at 25 Hz) starting at tick 625.
definition: Distinct active set with phys_gps absent; scenario gps_dropout injects a fix loss at t = 25 s for 8 s.
baseline: The same flight before onset: the pair is distinguishable.
counter_evidence: None. 200 ticks is exactly the 8 s injected window at 25 Hz.
alternative_explanation: The window could be an artefact of the bench simulator. Partly true and stated: this is the bench catalogue, not the WP-C4 injection campaign, and the two must not be conflated.

claim_text: Smoothing changes threshold-crossing behaviour, and the direction and size of the change depend on the arm.
definition: Instantaneous chi-square recovered by exact inversion of the comparator's EW smoother (round-trip error 0 to 1e-9); crossing = first tick past the mu0+3sigma0 threshold after onset.
baseline: Clean arm with no fault injected, same flight profile.
counter_evidence: On the clean arm the SAME threshold is crossed by both series, so the 'latency' there is a false alarm, not a detection. Reported.
alternative_explanation: Smoothing could simply add lag. Partly true: the lag is +0.12 s (slow ramp), +0.08 s (3 m/s spoof), +0.04 s (fast ramp) - it SHRINKS as the fault gets faster, which lag alone does not explain.

claim_text: In the pre-onset window smoothing cuts threshold crossings from 36 to 9 out of 374 ticks, a 4x reduction in false crossings.
definition: Window 5.0 s to 20.0 s; threshold mu0 + 3*sigma0 from csia/v1_1/sequential.py IN_CONTROL['gps'].
baseline: Instantaneous series on the same ticks.
counter_evidence: None. Identical in all four arms because the window precedes onset.
alternative_explanation: The threshold could be badly chosen. True and stated: a bare lambda threshold is not a usable detector, which is why the trust path and the CUSUM path (0 false alarms each) are reported beside it.

claim_text: The CUSUM alarms earlier than the trust threshold in every faulted arm and never in the clean window.
definition: CUSUM latencies after onset: 2.96 s (1 m/s), 1.16 s (3 m/s), 0.72 s (6 m/s) against trust 8.72 / 3.36 / 3.24 s. Clean arm: no alarm.
baseline: The frozen trust threshold FailsafeConfig.nav_caution = 0.75, reported BOTH raw and net of the 1.0 s policy dwell.
counter_evidence: None on these four arms. RED TEAM 2.3 was correct that the raw comparison flatters the CUSUM by one dwell period; detector-to-detector the figures are 2.96 vs 7.72, 1.16 vs 2.36 and 0.72 vs 2.24, so the conclusion survives. Coverage is limited: the bank has no residual for imu0, imu1 or baro, stated in sequential.py NO_RESIDUAL.
alternative_explanation: The CUSUM might be tuned to these arms. Excluded: k = 0.5 is textbook and h = 500 was fixed by a zero-clean-alarm rule before these arms existed.

claim_text: Mechanism B replicates on ArduPilot 4.8: given the platform's own measured banked state and measured per-tick evidence and forgetting factor, the source recursion reproduces the runtime trust trajectory and predicts the observed threshold crossing.
definition: PREREGISTERED before the first trial (blob 0e18611). Crossing at T* = 0.75; reconstruction error tolerance 1e-6; crossing-error tolerance 2 ticks.
baseline: CLEAN, STEP_SMALL and STEP_LARGE arms, 15 trials, all predeclared as non-crossing.
counter_evidence: None. 20/20 trials valid; reconstruction error 1.0e-15 to 2.0e-15 against a 1e-6 tolerance; crossing error 0 ticks on all 5 ramps; 0/5 control crossings.
alternative_explanation: The crossing tick differs from the 2015 ArduCopter 3.3 figure because the banked state differs. That is expected and predeclared: the mechanism replicates, not the number. Testing against 93.31 ticks would have produced a false non-replication.

counter_evidence: 0 trials run. The preregistration forbids substituting another intervention.
alternative_explanation: A substitute intervention would have tested a different fault and would not have been a replication. Recording INAPPLICABLE is the honest outcome.

claim_text: On 15,595 ticks from 20 real ArduPilot 4.8 SITL trials in which the GNSS fix was never lost, the structural predicate reports the nominal|gps_fault pair DISTINGUISHABLE at every tick and never collapses.
definition: D(nominal, gps_fault) = {phys_gps} intersect ACTIVE, evaluated per tick from the campaign gate_applicable column. A single collapse on a fix-preserving trial would falsify the account in MECHANISM_A.md; the test was declared before the run.
baseline: The bench catalogue, where the same predicate DOES collapse for 200 ticks under injected fix loss.
counter_evidence: None. 0 gate-closed ticks and 0 collapses across CLEAN (5100), RAMP (887) and STEP (9608).
alternative_explanation: This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL, not a replication of self-occlusion. Self-occlusion needs a fault that removes the fix, and no fix-loss arm exists on ArduPilot 4.8 in this repository. The trials are fix-preserving by their own validity criterion, so they CANNOT exhibit it, and none is claimed.
